clue.text: Fall to pieces and perish, concealing transgression to get back at informer

indicators.note: something concealing another holds it inside, so the word for perish wraps around the rest

parts.note: to perish is to die
a sin is a transgression

indicators.note: getting something back sends it the other way, so the word get is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written, before it is turned round
a rat is slang for an informer

explanation.surface: Someone collapsing and dying while hiding a sin, all to get revenge on a snitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get back' reads as taking revenge, but 'back' only turns 'get' round; the perishing word is broken open to hold everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To disintegrate is to break apart into fragments, which is exactly what falling to pieces describes.

clue.text: Fear poisonous adder

indicators.note: poison corrupts and spoils, so the letters of the next word are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Being afraid of a venomous snake.
explanation.walkthrough: An adder is a venomous snake, which makes 'poisonous' look purely descriptive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is deep apprehension or terror, a close synonym of fear.

clue.text: Uncouth louts seizing oil company is not the main story

indicators.note: uncouth means rough and unpolished, so the following word's letters are jumbled
seizing means grabbing and holding, so the jumble takes the company inside it

parts.note: the letters of louts rearranged, then split around the company
BP is the British oil company once called British Petroleum

explanation.surface: Thugs grabbing an oil firm is a sideshow, not the headline news.
explanation.walkthrough: BP was formerly British Petroleum. The definition includes 'is not', so the answer is read as the thing that is not the main story.
explanation.definitionFit: A subplot is a secondary storyline running alongside the main plot of a novel or film.

clue.text: Craft, then lorry, heading toward a pole

indicators.note: to craft is to fashion or build, so the following letters are shaped into a new word

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat and then a truck on an expedition to the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as a vessel, the first leg of a journey; it is an instruction to make something from 'then lorry'. A lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Northerly describes moving toward the north, and the North Pole lies in that direction.

clue.text: John's heartfelt online content

indicators.note: content is what a thing holds inside, so the answer sits within the letters of the preceding words

parts.note: the letters running across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A sincere social-media post from someone called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John's' is read as 'John is': the answer is the first name that goes before John, Elton John being the British pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton is the first name of the singer Elton John, so it is what precedes John in that name.

clue.text: Vile, ratty, disgusting entertainment

indicators.note: something disgusting is foul and corrupted, so the preceding letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters of both words to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict on some trashy, nasty, revolting show.
explanation.walkthrough: The three adjectives read as one sneering review, and the answer is the very genre the sneer suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality TV is a genre of unscripted television watched for amusement, so it is a kind of entertainment.

clue.text: Criminal rush to separate true from false

indicators.note: separating two things means coming between them, so this word goes in the middle

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for true, as in logic tables
hie is an old word for hurry or rush
F is the abbreviation for false

explanation.surface: A crook hurrying to tell truth from lies.
explanation.walkthrough: HIE sits between T and F; T and F are the true and false of a truth table.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is a person who steals, one particular kind of criminal.

clue.text: Lebanese-American writer and soldier introducing a type of muffin

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in ahead, so the soldier comes first and the muffin follows

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a bran muffin is a common type

explanation.surface: An author and a soldier presenting a new kind of muffin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kahlil Gibran, author of The Prophet, was a Lebanese-born writer who lived and worked in the United States.

clue.text: Came out for red-nosed revelry

indicators.note: revelry is wild partying, so the letters it acts on are thrown about

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: Someone emerged ready for a night of drunken partying, nose already glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came out for' reads as leaving the house for a party; here it means publicly backed.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out for a candidate or cause is to declare support publicly, which is what endorsing means.

clue.text: Leaders of Egypt might begin exporting refined coal

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A note on Egyptian rulers who may start shipping out purified coal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing piece of coal or wood left in a dying fire.

clue.text: Vicious rant about "stupid idiot"—that's what we get from our elders

definitions.text: that's what we get from our elders

indicators.note: something vicious is wild and savage, so the letters of rant are thrown into disorder
something stupid is muddled, so the letters of idiot come out in a confused order
about means around, so the first jumble surrounds the second

parts.note: the letters of rant rearranged, then split around the other piece
the letters of idiot rearranged

explanation.surface: Grandparents delivering a nasty rant about some stupid idiot, passed down as family wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are scrambled separately, one jumble then wrapping the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition is the set of customs and beliefs handed down from one generation to the next.

clue.text: Move laboriously westward, greeting nation's first mammal

indicators.note: in an across clue, westward means right to left, so that word is read backwards

parts.note: to plod is to move laboriously, read here before turning round
hi is a greeting

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of nation

explanation.surface: A creature trudging west and saluting the country's foremost mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nation' is a nod to the magazine that publishes this puzzle, but it is only there for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The dolphin is a marine animal that breathes air and suckles its young, so it is a mammal, not a fish.

clue.text: Deduce number in conflagration

parts.note: to infer is to deduce
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A detective working out a figure while a fire rages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but here it simply joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, fierce fire, and a conflagration is the same kind of blaze.

clue.text: Goodbye to partner, from the side

parts.note: 'later!' is a casual way to say goodbye
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Waving farewell to a spouse, glimpsed in profile.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways or toward the flank, which is coming from the side.

clue.text: Pines in a sauna? That's not very likely

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
a sauna is hot

explanation.surface: Pine trees growing inside a steam room would be an improbable sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' looks like trees; it is the verb, as in yearns.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is an attempt or outcome with little chance of success, an idiom for something improbable.

clue.text: Characteristic behavior: Elites fly all over the place

indicators.note: things flying all over the place are scattered, so the preceding letters land in a new order

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged together with fly
also part of the fodder as well as the signal

explanation.surface: The rich jet around the globe as a matter of habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' does double duty: its letters join the fodder while 'fly all over the place' signals the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifestyle is the typical way a person or group lives, their habitual pattern of conduct.

clue.text: Reflect, my boy — I'm an ancient king

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the words that follow are read backwards

parts.note: my boy is my son
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A boastful father telling his son to think it over, since he is royalty of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflect' reads like 'think it over', but it is the signal to read the following words backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Minos was the legendary king of Crete in Greek myth, owner of the Minotaur's labyrinth.

clue.text: Bodybuilder announced a mollusk-themed superhero?

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the answer is spelt as the phrase that follows sounds

parts.note: a hero named after the shellfish, a mussel, would be Mussel Man

explanation.surface: A gym-goer is introduced as a comic-book hero based on shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussels are shellfish; the question mark flags the invented superhero.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscleman is a man with highly developed muscles, typically from weight training.

clue.text: An overturned farmyard enclosure is gross

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in this word the letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written, before it is flipped
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A tipped-over pigpen is a disgusting sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'An' is overturned; the sty stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross in its slang sense means disgusting or repellent, a synonym of nasty.

clue.text: Show hide

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to display a film or programme
second meaning: to conceal behind a partition

explanation.walkthrough: The two words are opposites, yet one verb serves both: you screen a movie and screen something from view.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers projecting a film to an audience and also shielding something from sight.

clue.text: Loud American composer gets recognized, like the Department of Defense's headquarters

definitions.text: like the Department of Defense's headquarters

parts.note: f (forte) is the musical marking for loud
Charles Ives was an American modernist composer
ID'd, identified, spelt without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A noisy American composer earns recognition, like the Pentagon.
explanation.walkthrough: IDED is ID'd, meaning identified or recognized.
explanation.definitionFit: The Department of Defense is housed in the Pentagon, a building with five sides.

clue.text: Office employment: storing dirty jokes in database

indicators.note: dirty means soiled and messed up, so the following letters are jumbled
something storing another keeps it inside, so the abbreviation surrounds the jumble

parts.note: DB is the standard abbreviation for database, split around the rest
the letters of jokes rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at work keeping a file of smutty jokes on the company system.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk job is work done sitting in an office, as opposed to physical or outdoor work.

clue.text: Holy person travels on horseback, or walks with determination

parts.note: St. is the abbreviation for saint
someone who rides travels on horseback

explanation.surface: A saint either rides a horse or marches along purposefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Striding means taking long, decisive steps, which is walking with determination.

clue.text: Radio personality working outside one city in France

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the first two pieces wrap around the numeral

parts.note: a DJ is a disc jockey on the radio
I is the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A radio presenter working away from a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' reads as location in the surface; it tells you to put the radio host and the working word around the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Dijon is the capital of Burgundy, famous for its mustard.

clue.text: Aimless, wandering woman

indicators.note: something wandering strays from its course, so the letters of the preceding word move out of place

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drifting, purposeless lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aimless' and 'wandering' look like a pair describing the woman, but the first is the fodder and the second rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Melissa is a common female first name, so it stands for a woman by example.

clue.text: Poem written in two meters — that's how some people communicate

indicators.note: something written in another sits inside it, so the poem goes between the two units

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for meter, taken twice and split
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A verse composed in a mix of two rhythms, which is how certain people express themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meters' looks like poetic rhythm, a fitting partner for 'Poem'; it is the unit of length, M.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is a device that links computers over phone lines, letting people exchange messages online.

clue.text: Edge of African lake where eagles live

indicators.note: an edge is the outermost border, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of African
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: The shore of an African lake, home to eagles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African lake' reads as one place, but the lake is Erie in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerie is the nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, built high on a cliff.

clue.text: Very happy, OJ drove recklessly around you once

indicators.note: a reckless drive is out of control, so these letters are thrown about
around means surrounding, so the jumble goes outside the old pronoun

parts.note: the letters of OJ and drove rearranged, then split around the pronoun
ye is the old, once-common word for you

explanation.surface: An ecstatic O.J. careering wildly around someone, recalling the notorious Bronco chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove' reads as the past of drive in a car-chase picture; it is part of the fodder. 'Once' marks an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Overjoyed means extremely pleased, a stronger synonym for happy.

clue.text: Officer repelled crowd with zero resistance

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a jam is a crowd packed tight
O looks like the digit zero
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A police officer pushed back the mob without meeting any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd' tempts as MOB; it is JAM, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A major is a commissioned military officer ranking above a captain.

clue.text: Put in the ground, and ready to be taken out of the ground — it's endless

parts.note: to inter is to bury

parts.words: ready to be taken out of the ground
parts.note: a seam that is minable can be dug out of the earth

explanation.surface: Something buried and then ready to be dug up again, a cycle without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Interminable means seeming to go on forever, i.e. without end.
